* Test data for parsing Bazel compilation output

#+PROPERTY: header-args :mkdirp yes :main no

#+BEGIN_SRC bazel-module :tangle MODULE.bazel
bazel_dep(name = "rules_cc", version = "0.2.17")
#+END_SRC

#+BEGIN_SRC bazel-build :tangle package/BUILD
load("@rules_cc//cc:cc_library.bzl", "cc_library")

cc_library(
    name = "test",
    srcs = ["test.cc"],
    deprecation = "Deprecated!",
)
#+END_SRC

#+BEGIN_SRC C++ :tangle package/test.cc
UnknownType foo;
#+END_SRC

** Merged standard output and error from Bazel

To make the test hermetic, we generate Bazel output statically and tangle the
output when running the test.  Execute this code block with =C-c C-v C-e= to
regenerate the Bazel output:

#+BEGIN_SRC elisp :var org=(buffer-file-name) dir=(make-temp-file "t" t) :wrap "src fundamental :tangle bazel.out"
;; Set up a basic repository layout in the temporary directory.
(let ((temp (expand-file-name ".tangle.org" dir)))
  (copy-file org temp)
  (with-temp-buffer
    (insert-file-contents temp :visit)
    (after-find-file)
    (org-babel-tangle)))

(with-temp-buffer
  ;; We explicitly compile with the current directory set to a subdirectory to
  ;; ensure that repository-relative filenames still work as expected.
  (let ((default-directory (file-name-as-directory
                            (expand-file-name "package" dir))))
    ;; Ignore the exit status of “bazel build” because we expect it to fail.
    ;; We can’t use --quiet here because that would also suppress the
    ;; deprecation warning.
    (process-file "bazel" nil t nil "--nohome_rc" "build"
                  "--attempt_to_print_relative_paths"
                  "--noshow_progress" "--noshow_loading_progress"
                  "//..."))
  (delete-directory dir :recursive)
  (buffer-string))
#+END_SRC
